title: Flight delayed or cancelled: how to claim

can_you_claim.q: Where did the flight depart from, or which airline operated it?
can_you_claim.UK: UK departure (any airline) or UK/EU airline arriving in the UK: UK261 applies.
can_you_claim.EU: EU departure (any airline) or EU airline arriving in the EU: EU261 applies.
can_you_claim.US: No federal compensation right. You can claim a refund (see rights).

can_you_claim.q: How late did you arrive, or was the flight cancelled?
can_you_claim.answer: 3+ hours late on arrival, or cancelled, opens compensation under UK261/EU261.

can_you_claim.q: Was it caused by 'extraordinary circumstances' (e.g. weather, air traffic control)?
can_you_claim.answer: If yes, no compensation, but care and refund rights remain. Most technical faults and airline-staff strikes do not count as extraordinary (EU page).

UK.escalation: Complain to airline; if unresolved after final response or 8 weeks, go to the airline's ADR provider, or CAA PACT if the airline has none.
UK.time_limit: NOT STATED BY CAA: verify limitation period before publishing

EU.threshold: Arrive 3+ hours late (4h for the €600 tier on some non-EU flights); cancellation notified under 14 days before departure
EU.care: Meals, 2 calls/messages, hotel + transport if overnight. Refund option at 5h+ departure delay.
EU.escalation: Airline first; no reply in 2 months -> national enforcement body; ADR; European Small Claims.
EU.time_limit: Set by each country's national limitation rules (no single number)

US.refund: Full refund (incl. taxes/fees) if the airline cancels or significantly changes the flight and you decline the alternative. Significant change: >3h domestic, >6h international.
US.baggage: Checked-bag fee refund if bag not delivered within 12h (domestic) / 15-30h (international).
US.timeline: Card payments: within 7 business days. Other methods: within 20 calendar days.
US.no_compensation_note: Rule covers refunds only, not compensation. DOT has a separate proposal on compensation: check status before publishing.
